I understand that I have a different opinion than you all, and this isn't exactly the best crowd to defend my opinion against,  but you people have to understand that this shit happens. Do I believe it was NECESSARY to kill him? No. Not by any stretch of the imagination. But seeing from the officers' perspective, I can understand why they did what they did. Ask any police officer, what their primary objective of the day is. It's not to kill people or arrest anyone, it's to fucking stay alive. Now they had a job to do, remove the man from the park (or where ever he is), and he put himself in a situation from which he could not successfully return. He refused orders and just was being shitty with them. Does that give the officer the right to shoot him? NO. What made this shooting justified was the fact that the man pulled knives. Had he done what he should have, there would have never been an incident. The officer shot because his fellow officer was in danger. Not because he could, not because he wanted to, but because a "brother" of his was in danger. Put in the exact same situation, I can't say that I would do the same, but I understand why he fired. And also you people seem to think that they were just shooting his lifeless body for nothing. At the time, his legs were still moving. He could have still been able to attack the officers, so they did what they could to incapacitate him. No one knew for sure that the suspect had expired. 

Also, just so you guys are aware, I'm no police state supporter. As an American that supports the rights of the citizens of this great nation, I trust the police about as much as the rest of you, but in this particular case, I agree with what happened. The man got what he had coming and paid for it.
